title: A Glial Cell That Stops Respiring

scenes.tts: If a glial cell stopped burning fuel in its mitochondria, would the axon it wraps starve?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Glial Cell That Stops Respiring. A glial wrap around an axon; the glial cell's mitochondria dim.
scenes.narration: If a glial cell stopped burning fuel in its mitochondria, would the axon it wraps starve?

scenes.tts: Start with a puzzle. Mice lacking the myelin protein P L P, or the enzyme C N P, made close to normal myelin.
scenes.caption: Start with a puzzle. Mice lacking the myelin protein PLP, or the enzyme CNP, made close to normal myelin.
scenes.visual: Two electron-micrograph-style cross-sections, each a normal-looking ring of myelin. Credits: Griffiths and colleagues, 1998 (PLP); Lappe-Siefke and colleagues, 2003 (CNP).
scenes.narration: Start with a puzzle. Mice lacking the myelin protein PLP, or the enzyme CNP, made close to normal myelin.

scenes.tts: Yet as they aged, their axons swelled and degenerated. The glial cell seems to give the axon more than insulation.
scenes.visual: The axons inside the normal-looking rings swell. Label: with age. Card: something besides insulation.
scenes.narration: Yet as they aged, their axons swelled and degenerated. The glial cell seems to give the axon more than insulation.

scenes.tts: Fuel is one candidate. Glycolysis turns glucose into pyruvate. Pyruvate can enter the mitochondrion, for far more A T P.
scenes.caption: Fuel is one candidate. Glycolysis turns glucose into pyruvate. Pyruvate can enter the mitochondrion, for far more ATP.
scenes.visual: Glucose splits into two pyruvate with 2 ATP. Route 1: pyruvate enters a mitochondrion; the citric acid cycle turns and ATP pours out.
scenes.narration: Fuel is one candidate. Glycolysis turns glucose into pyruvate. Pyruvate can enter the mitochondrion, for far more ATP.

scenes.tts: Or it can become lactate. That turns N A D H back into N A D plus, so glycolysis keeps running without mitochondria. Another cell can turn lactate back and burn it.
scenes.visual: Route 2: pyruvate becomes lactate and NAD+ is regenerated. Lactate leaves through an MCT, enters a second cell, becomes pyruvate and enters that cell's mitochondrion.
scenes.narration: Or it can become lactate. That turns NADH back into NAD+, so glycolysis keeps running without mitochondria. Another cell can turn lactate back and burn it.
scenes.caption: Or it can become lactate. That turns NADH back into NAD+, so glycolysis keeps running without mitochondria. Another cell can turn lactate back and burn it.

scenes.tts: A cell that stops at lactate keeps only two A T P. Its lactates carry more than nine tenths of what the glucose could yield.
scenes.caption: A cell that stops at lactate keeps only 2 ATP. Its lactates carry more than nine-tenths of what the glucose could yield.
scenes.visual: ATP tally on screen: glucose burned fully, about 30 to 32 ATP. The glial cell keeps 2. The two lactates carry about 28 to 30. Label: portable fuel.
scenes.narration: A cell that stops at lactate keeps only 2 ATP. Its lactates carry more than nine-tenths of what the glucose could yield.

scenes.tts: Now the test. One laboratory deleted the gene Cox ten in myelinating cells. Without it, they can make A T P only by glycolysis.
scenes.caption: Now the test. One laboratory deleted the gene Cox10 in myelinating cells. Without it, they can make ATP only by glycolysis.
scenes.visual: Credit: Fünfschilling, Nave and colleagues, 2012. Cox10 is snipped out in glial cells only. The respiratory chain loses complex IV once the existing complex wears out. Label: glycolysis only.
scenes.narration: Now the test. One laboratory deleted the gene Cox10 in myelinating cells. Without it, they can make ATP only by glycolysis.

scenes.tts: If oligodendrocytes must respire to keep axons healthy, what should happen in the adult brain over the following months?
scenes.visual: Pause and predict card: must they respire? What happens over months?
scenes.narration: If oligodendrocytes must respire to keep axons healthy, what should happen in the adult brain over the following months?

scenes.tts: If they had to respire, myelin and axons should fail. Instead, the oligodendrocytes survived. Myelin and axons were largely preserved for months.
scenes.visual: Faint expected picture of thinning myelin and swollen axons, replaced by the result: oligodendrocyte, myelin and axon all stay. Three green ticks. Label: adult CNS, the months followed.
scenes.narration: If they had to respire, myelin and axons should fail. Instead, the oligodendrocytes survived. Myelin and axons were largely preserved for months.

scenes.tts: Oligodendrocytes that have made their myelin can live on glycolysis alone. Pyruvate and lactate they cannot burn must leave or be left over. Leaving would fit glia feeding axons, but this does not show it.
scenes.visual: Card: glia can live on glycolysis; axons do not need glial respiration. Question on the glial cell: lactate and pyruvate it cannot burn, where do they go? A dashed arrow from glia to axon, labelled fits, not shown.
scenes.narration: Oligodendrocytes that have made their myelin can live on glycolysis alone. Pyruvate and lactate they cannot burn must leave or be left over. Leaving would fit glia feeding axons, but this does not show it.

scenes.tts: Peripheral nerves differed. Schwann cells without Cox ten survived but failed to myelinate properly. The mice developed a severe neuropathy.
scenes.caption: Peripheral nerves differed. Schwann cells without Cox10 survived but failed to myelinate properly. The mice developed a severe neuropathy.
scenes.visual: A peripheral nerve cross-section with thin or missing myelin; a red cross on the nerve. Label: severe neuropathy.
scenes.narration: Peripheral nerves differed. Schwann cells without Cox10 survived but failed to myelinate properly. The mice developed a severe neuropathy.

scenes.tts: Those cells were still building myelin, a costly stage. They survived, but needed respiration to myelinate. The stage may explain part of the difference.
scenes.visual: A living Schwann cell dividing and winding new myelin, with an energy meter running high; the wrap stays thin. Labels: still myelinating; cell survives; stage may be part of the reason.
scenes.narration: Those cells were still building myelin, a costly stage. They survived, but needed respiration to myelinate. The stage may explain part of the difference.

scenes.tts: One more clue. A scan that measures brain chemicals found extra lactate in the mutants, but only under anesthesia. Within an hour after the anesthetic ended, it fell below detection.
scenes.caption: One more clue. A scan that measures brain chemicals found extra lactate in the mutants, but only under anaesthesia. Within an hour after the anaesthetic ended, it fell below detection.
scenes.visual: A magnetic resonance spectroscopy trace: a lactate peak rises in the mutant beside an anaesthesia icon, then sinks to baseline when the icon is removed. Clock: within an hour.
scenes.narration: One more clue. A scan that measures brain chemicals found extra lactate in the mutants, but only under anaesthesia. Within an hour after the anaesthetic ended, it fell below detection.

scenes.tts: Why would it show up only under anesthesia?
scenes.caption: Why would it show up only under anaesthesia?
scenes.visual: Pause and predict card: why only under anaesthesia?
scenes.narration: Why would it show up only under anaesthesia?

scenes.tts: One reading: glycolytic glia make more lactate than they burn. Awake, something uses it as fast as it is made. Under anesthesia, that use slows.
scenes.caption: One reading: glycolytic glia make more lactate than they burn. Awake, something uses it as fast as it is made. Under anaesthesia, that use slows.
scenes.visual: Lactate flows out of the glial cell and is used at once; under the anaesthesia icon, use slows and lactate piles up. Label: one reading.
scenes.narration: One reading: glycolytic glia make more lactate than they burn. Awake, something uses it as fast as it is made. Under anaesthesia, that use slows.

scenes.tts: The axons are an obvious candidate user. But the experiment never traced where the lactate went.
scenes.visual: A question mark on the axon; a dashed arrow from glia to axon, labelled not traced.
scenes.narration: The axons are an obvious candidate user. But the experiment never traced where the lactate went.

scenes.tts: So switch off the glial cell's respiration, and the axon in the brain is spared, over the months studied.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: respiration switched off, CNS axon spared over the months studied.
scenes.narration: So switch off the glial cell's respiration, and the axon in the brain is spared, over the months studied.
